opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jacob Santos (employee ID E050) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E050.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jacob Santos (E050) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, write is permitted (role owns Source Code, so admin is also allowed). Requested level write is within policy; recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security record for E050 shows contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors with basic training may have at most read access; write is not permitted. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so recommend read for Source Code.
reason: The two notes about E050 conflict on employment type: one lists full-time Engineer (which would allow write), while the Security record lists contractor with basic security training, which per policy caps access at read. Given the conflicting records, I apply the more restrictive valid interpretation: contractor with basic training may not exceed read. Requested write exceeds that maximum, so grant the maximum of read.
